findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(B) Cooling. (B) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours to 5°C (41°F) or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature, such as reconstituted FOODS and canned tuna. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the follow nonfood-contact surfaces in need of more frequent cleaning:
(i) the underside of the soda fountain where several residues have accumulated;
(ii) the hose going into the fan in the walk-in cooler where a significant amount of ice has accumulated.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of residues by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing (THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION). Additionally, several times during the inspection employees almost re-entered the kitchen or put on gloves without handwashing but the PIC intervened and instructed them to wash hands. The PIC should focus on hand washing education for all employees. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there are several holes in the mop sink wall. These holes must be filled (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. The PIC stated that an employee had dumped the bucket after lunch but it was not remade. A sanitizer bucket was filled during the inspection testing at 400 ppm (quat). Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the fans in the walk-in cooler (THIS IS A FIRST REPAET VIOLATION) and walk-in freezer have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to the sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there is not employee health reporting forms at the facility. There needs to be employee reporting forms signed by the employees stating they will report to the PIC about their health and activities related to diseases transmissible through food. The inspector provided employee reporting forms to the PIC. Ensure these forms are signed by all employees before the follow-up date of 07/08/2024.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed that an employee turned off the faucet handles with their barehand after washing their hands. Failure to use a barrier to turn off the faucet handles recontaminates clean hands. The inspector talked to the PIC and they will educated their employees on the proper hand-washing procedure. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed that the inside top-potion of the ice machine surrounding the baffles has an accumulation of soil, including pink mold. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. A follow-up on 07/08/2024 will occur to ensure that the accumulation of soil and mold in the ice machine has been cleaned.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the following needs cleaned inside of the walk-in cooler: (1) dust on the blades of the fan; (2) soil on the floors. Ensure that these surfaces inside the walk-in cooler are cleaned at a frequently necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil and mold underneath the ice machine. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. There is a leak occurring from the ice machine that could be contributing to the mold build-up. During the 07/08/2024 follow-up, inspectors will be checking up on the soil and mold beneath the ice machine. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC did not have food handler certificates for the employees. Ensure that all employees get their food handlers certification within 30 days of hiring, and that copies of all the certificates are held at the facility.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
